images.caption: Figure 2:ReasonText addresses gaps in existing TAISR benchmarks.(a) SA-Text-test assigns difficulty at the image level via three degradation strengths, which does not indicate whether each instance requires reasoning. (b) ReasonText instead labels each instance with a perception-grounded difficulty level, separating reasoning-required from locally recoverable text. (c) ReasonText is constructed from human annotations, which remain reliable across diverse scenes. (d) ReasonText crops the image to preserve context needed to read reasoning-required text.

Figure 3:Gemma 4 reads locally illegible text by reasoning over relevant cues.Top: given only the target region (the locally illegible "4"), Gemma 4 fails. Adding random unrelated patches does not help, but adding the related numeric column "1"–"8" restores the correct reading. Bottom: likewise, "WHEY" is read only when the banner "70% BETTER THAN WHEY" is visible. Blue and red backgrounds mark correct and incorrect readings.

Figure 4:Qualitative results of RTC across reasoning types.For Level 2 instances of each reasoning type, the top and bottom rows show the outputs of six text-conditioned SR models without and with RTC, respectively. With RTC, some models can turn incorrect text into correct text.

images.caption: Figure A:Computing GTTCA on a restored text instance.Each text instance is cropped around its GT polygon with padding, rotated and flipped with its GT orientation, and recognized by an OCR model. The recognized text is compared with the GT transcript under normalized exact match.

Figure B:SR models fail on reasoning-required text.Outputs of the twelve SR models on one Level 1 (locally recoverable) instance and three Level 2 (reasoning-required) instances, one for each cue.Blueandredborders on the SR outputs mark correct and incorrect restorations. On Level 1, most models restore “Crab” correctly. On Level 2, most models fail to restore the text.

header: Appendix BAdditional Details on Reasoning Transfer via Captioning

images.caption: Figure C:Overview of Reasoning Transfer via Captioning (RTC).(1) Caption by reasoning: a frozen MLLM reads the LR image under the reasoning prompt and returns a two-sentence caption with a scene description and the inferred transcripts. (2) Restore by conditioning: a frozen text-conditioned SR model restores the LR image with this caption in place of its default caption.
